claims.statement: Persistent unexplained kidney-allograft dysfunction warrants tissue evaluation before antirejection treatment when sampling is clinically suitable.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Graft biopsy with appropriate viral/complement stains and concurrent donor-specific antibody assessment helps distinguish causes of graft dysfunction.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Interstitial inflammation with tubulitis is compatible with cellular rejection only after relevant infectious and other findings are considered.
claims.limitation: Tubulitis does not by itself distinguish BK inflammation from T-cell rejection; no Banff grade is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Corticosteroids are initial treatment for acute cellular kidney-allograft rejection.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Lymphocyte-depleting treatment may be considered for refractory cellular rejection after reassessment.
claims.limitation: Conditional recommendation; no automatic escalation from one creatinine result or universal steroid course.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Urinary BK replication prompts plasma viral assessment; urinary detection is not equivalent to plasma DNAemia or biopsy-proven nephropathy.
claims.limitation: Single current consensus publication; no urine or plasma cutoff is introduced.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Compatible tubular viral changes with positive polyomavirus large-T-antigen staining and BK replication support BK nephropathy.
claims.limitation: SV40 large-T-antigen stain cross-reacts with polyomaviruses; the scenario also supplies BK plasma detection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: For biopsy-proven BK nephropathy without concurrent rejection or high immunologic risk, reduction of maintenance immunosuppression is the principal treatment.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Leflunomide and cidofovir are not recommended routine treatment for BK nephropathy.
claims.limitation: One current consensus; no claim that no experimental treatment can ever be considered.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Rising creatinine during BK treatment can reflect different processes; tissue reassessment can inform suspected concurrent rejection.
claims.limitation: No automatic inference of rejection from falling plasma BK or from tubulitis during active infection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Clarithromycin can raise tacrolimus exposure through CYP3A inhibition.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Tacrolimus can cause renal dysfunction and tremor; elevated trough exposure with toxicity may require dose reduction or temporary interruption.
claims.limitation: Exact named-label fact; transplant team determines the actual adjustment. No target range is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Tacrolimus exposure monitoring uses a trough specimen; a sample drawn after a dose cannot be interpreted as the scheduled predose trough.
claims.limitation: Sampling chronology is constructed. No formulation conversion or exact post-dose sampling interval is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Tacrolimus binds FKBP12 and inhibits calcineurin-dependent T-cell activation.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: PTLD requires adequate tissue pathology for diagnosis and classification; EBV blood DNA and imaging do not replace tissue assessment.
claims.limitation: AST support is exact local offline reuse; current licensed review cross-check. No biopsy-method or processing preference inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: A falling or absent blood EBV signal does not resolve an enlarging lesion suspicious for PTLD.
claims.limitation: Qualitative inference from tissue diagnostic requirement and EBV heterogeneity; no blood cutoff or response criterion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Reducing immunosuppression is an initial component of PTLD care when balanced against graft risk.
claims.limitation: No fixed taper, withdrawal order or percentage; joint transplant/hematology planning required.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Rituximab is a treatment option for CD20-positive B-cell PTLD requiring therapy after reduction of immunosuppression.
claims.limitation: Current licensed narrative review only freshly readable; primary management corroboration is still required. No standalone algorithm or sequence-to-chemotherapy rule approved.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Gastrointestinal CMV can occur with undetectable plasma DNA; tissue histology and CMV immunohistochemistry establish tissue-invasive disease.
claims.limitation: Current consensus, particularly relevant in seropositive recipients; no assay cutoff or sensitivity estimate.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Severe CMV disease or unreliable oral absorption favors intravenous ganciclovir; oral valganciclovir is suitable for clinically appropriate oral-tolerant disease.
claims.limitation: One current consensus; adult patient-specific renal adjustment required, with no doses or duration authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Leukopenia during ganciclovir treatment should prompt review of other marrow-suppressive therapies or growth-factor support rather than antiviral underdosing based on leukopenia itself.
claims.limitation: One current consensus; renal function still governs dose adjustment, and severe cytopenia requires specialist assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Mycophenolate can contribute to marrow suppression.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: A transfusion can change a candidate HLA-antibody profile; compatibility assessment must consider sensitizing events after the tested specimen.
claims.limitation: Current society guidance; no specific timing interval or US allocation policy imported.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Antibody concern for an offered donor depends on the recipient antibody specificities and donor HLA antigens, rather than kinship by itself.
claims.limitation: Select the donor with no represented antibody target for further workup; no claim of final safety from bead testing.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: ABO blood-group compatibility and HLA/crossmatch testing assess separate compatibility questions.
claims.limitation: No donor subtype exception, titration threshold, or ABO-incompatible transplant exclusion is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Starting an mTOR inhibitor should be deferred until graft function is established and surgical wounds have healed.
claims.limitation: No exact perioperative hold or restart schedule; case concerns early post-transplant initiation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Mycophenolate exposure in pregnancy increases risks of pregnancy loss and congenital malformations.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Mycophenolate should be replaced or discontinued under transplant supervision before pregnancy attempts; azathioprine is a described substitute.
claims.limitation: No universal pregnancy eligibility, washout interval or patient-specific medication prescription is approved.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Allopurinol inhibits a pathway of azathioprine inactivation, increasing risk of myelotoxicity.
claims.limitation: KDIGO advises avoiding this combination; labeling permits specialist dose modification. These are distinct approaches, not a contradiction resolved by a fabricated dose.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Pre-existing donor-reactive antibodies can cause rapid graft microvascular injury, distinct from newly generated antibody or cellular rejection.
claims.limitation: A clinical mechanism inference requires corroborating immune, tissue and specimen-timing findings, not early graft dysfunction alone.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Microvascular inflammation, complement-associated antibody interaction and donor-specific antibodies can support active antibody-mediated rejection.
claims.limitation: No Banff numeric score; actual diagnosis integrates complete tissue and serology, including mixed processes.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Plasma exchange and IVIG are a consensus treatment backbone for acute active antibody-mediated rejection.
claims.limitation: Weak efficacy evidence; no optimal regimen or use in chronic active AMR asserted. Requires current specialist review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Persisting delayed kidney-graft function can warrant biopsy despite patent vessels and adequate urinary drainage.
claims.limitation: No invented day threshold. Delayed graft function does not itself diagnose rejection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: A graft with represented acute tubular injury and recovering function does not require antirejection escalation solely because dialysis was needed.
claims.limitation: Inference from cause-directed graft evaluation; single guideline framework, not an exact dialysis or rejection-treatment protocol.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Early calcineurin-inhibitor therapy need not be delayed until kidney-graft function is established.
claims.limitation: KDIGO 2.2.1 and Renal Association 3.3 support early initiation. Not a rule to continue through proven toxicity or ignore institution-specific induction strategies.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult transplant recipients in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: CMV-specific cellular-immunity assays inform selected risk and prophylaxis decisions rather than diagnose a symptomatic gastrointestinal lesion.
claims.limitation: One current consensus; no universal assay cutoff or prophylaxis-stopping algorithm authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult transplant recipients in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Letermovir is not recommended as monotherapy for treatment of active CMV disease.
claims.limitation: One current consensus; distinguish active treatment from selected prophylaxis use.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult transplant recipients in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Febuxostat also inhibits xanthine oxidase, and concomitant use with azathioprine is not recommended in the label.
claims.limitation: No comparative gout ranking is taught; the boundary is the thiopurine interaction.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult transplant recipients in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Aggressive vascular cellular rejection can alter the choice between initial corticosteroids and lymphocyte-depleting treatment.
claims.limitation: Arterial sampling and the absence of intimal inflammation are constructed specimen observations, not inferred from negative capillary findings. No Banff score is assigned; RA 4.10 and KDIGO 6.3-6.4 delimit the treatment boundary.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: A tacrolimus result must be interpreted with actual dose and sample timing and the clinical course before changing the monitored regimen.
claims.limitation: The no-immediate-change plan is a bounded application to a mistimed specimen with stable represented renal and symptom findings, not a universal instruction to ignore high values or suspected toxicity.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: After improvement on intravenous ganciclovir, an adult who tolerates oral therapy can continue treatment with valganciclovir; oral delivery is preferred when clinically feasible for non-life-threatening disease.
claims.limitation: One current consensus, CMV treatment section and stepdown recommendation. Continued IV therapy is possible; the comparison concerns the preferred feasible route after recovery, with patient-specific renal dosing.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Clinical improvement or a change in delivery route does not alone complete CMV treatment; treatment-level exposure continues until the appropriate clinical and laboratory endpoint is reached.
claims.limitation: One current consensus; no universal viral-load threshold or exact duration is authored. The scenarios explicitly retain quantifiable DNA above the local endpoint.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Mycophenolate labeling supports interruption or reduction with appropriate evaluation when the absolute neutrophil count is below 1.3 ? 10^3/?L.
claims.limitation: Direct regulatory label sections 2.5 and 5.4. The constructed ANC 0.8-1.0 ? 10^9/L is below that stated boundary. A temporary hold is one supported option, not a universal dose/hold duration or proof of sole causation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: A donor-directed physical HLA crossmatch evaluates recipient serum against donor lymphocytes; it must be interpreted with the broader antibody assessment.
claims.limitation: TSANZ 7.2-7.3. The constructed recipient-cell pairing addresses a different target; no standardized autologous-control protocol, assay sensitivity, mandatory allocation assay or final acceptance rule is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Preconception transplant planning considers current graft stability on pregnancy-compatible medication, not elapsed time or substitution of one drug by itself.
claims.limitation: Guideline 5.1.1 and KDIGO 25.2.1. Constructed serial deterioration motivates reassessment; no automatic approval, mandatory immediate drug switch, eligibility threshold or washout interval is claimed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Sirolimus and everolimus are avoided when planning pregnancy when alternative treatment options exist.
claims.limitation: Pregnancy guideline 2.7 and KDIGO 25.2.3; limited human safety evidence. No washout duration or comparative graft-regimen preference is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Group O plasma normally contains anti-A and anti-B antibodies.
claims.limitation: Government ABO identity verification only. This does not establish an individual recipient titer or prove that ABO antibodies caused a particular graft event.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Anti-A and anti-B antibodies can be measured separately to assess the relevant ABO antibody state.
claims.limitation: Narrow primary-method verification from a small study. No method, reagent, titer cutoff, diagnostic sensitivity or transplant protocol is copied or preferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Plasma exchange can change circulating anti-ABO antibody levels, so a post-exchange specimen is not interchangeable with a pre-exchange specimen for reconstructing the earlier state.
claims.limitation: Qualitative pre/post relationship only, directly observed in a small primary cohort. No modeled change, kinetics, volume, removal fraction or universal timing requirement is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: KDIGO suggests interval allograft biopsy every 7-10 days during delayed graft function.
claims.limitation: Direct older KDIGO 9.3 suggestion, graded 2C. Only one adequate source for this exact interval was used. Days 3 and 11 are constructed observations illustrating serial reassessment, not a mandatory universal biopsy schedule; current transplant-service judgment remains required.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Ganciclovir and valganciclovir have different treatment and prevention dosing uses; a prevention strategy is not a substitute for an unfinished active CMV treatment course.
claims.limitation: One current consensus; no dosing table, exact dose or secondary-prophylaxis duration is reproduced. Secondary prophylaxis after treatment is not routine and requires a separate risk assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult kidney-transplant recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

withheldTeachingPoints.reason: Future CD20-positive PTLD treatment objective remains an unkeyed planning slot pending a fresh readable primary management source; no scored node or key is authored.
Priority gap retained: direct current comparative guidance for thrombosis, leak and rescue is not yet verified; no exact rescue timing/procedure authored.
Do not teach acute active AMR regimen as an established treatment for chronic active AMR; evidence differs.

The available atoms support general reduction but do not establish a unique sequence or magnitude when active rejection competes. Inventing a treatment response, regimen priority or CD20 escalation would exceed that support; without the graft conflict it remains the same one-association item returned by review.
withheldTeachingPoints.nextAction: Readable primary guidance for the specific disease-versus-graft tradeoff, transplant/hematology clinical judgment and another independent review; keep the CD20 planning hold.

withheldTeachingPoints.reason: The represented antigen panel supports matching a donor target but not a unique harder workup or acceptance decision. A current-versus-historical assay/threshold extension overlaps recorded assay/allocation holds and needs direct support. The balanced matrix removes convergence but does not create a second consequential inference.
withheldTeachingPoints.nextAction: A directly supported donor-specific workup boundary and exact clinical review, or manager-approved foundational exception; no such exception is claimed.

claims.statement: Persistent unexplained kidney-allograft dysfunction warrants tissue evaluation before antirejection treatment when sampling is clinically suitable.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Graft biopsy with appropriate viral/complement stains and concurrent donor-specific antibody assessment helps distinguish causes of graft dysfunction.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Interstitial inflammation with tubulitis is compatible with cellular rejection only after relevant infectious and other findings are considered.
claims.limitation: Tubulitis does not by itself distinguish BK inflammation from T-cell rejection; no Banff grade is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Corticosteroids are initial treatment for acute cellular kidney-allograft rejection.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Lymphocyte-depleting treatment may be considered for refractory cellular rejection after reassessment.
claims.limitation: Conditional recommendation; no automatic escalation from one creatinine result or universal steroid course.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Urinary BK replication prompts plasma viral assessment; urinary detection is not equivalent to plasma DNAemia or biopsy-proven nephropathy.
claims.limitation: Single current consensus publication; no urine or plasma cutoff is introduced.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Compatible tubular viral changes with positive polyomavirus large-T-antigen staining and BK replication support BK nephropathy.
claims.limitation: SV40 large-T-antigen stain cross-reacts with polyomaviruses; the scenario also supplies BK plasma detection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: For biopsy-proven BK nephropathy without concurrent rejection or high immunologic risk, reduction of maintenance immunosuppression is the principal treatment.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Leflunomide and cidofovir are not recommended routine treatment for BK nephropathy.
claims.limitation: One current consensus; no claim that no experimental treatment can ever be considered.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Rising creatinine during BK treatment can reflect different processes; tissue reassessment can inform suspected concurrent rejection.
claims.limitation: No automatic inference of rejection from falling plasma BK or from tubulitis during active infection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Clarithromycin can raise tacrolimus exposure through CYP3A inhibition.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Tacrolimus can cause renal dysfunction and tremor; elevated trough exposure with toxicity may require dose reduction or temporary interruption.
claims.limitation: Exact named-label fact; transplant team determines the actual adjustment. No target range is authored.

claims.statement: Tacrolimus exposure monitoring uses a trough specimen; a sample drawn after a dose cannot be interpreted as the scheduled predose trough.

claims.statement: Tacrolimus binds FKBP12 and inhibits calcineurin-dependent T-cell activation.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: PTLD requires adequate tissue pathology for diagnosis and classification; EBV blood DNA and imaging do not replace tissue assessment.
claims.limitation: AST support is exact local offline reuse; current licensed review cross-check. No biopsy-method or processing preference inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: A falling or absent blood EBV signal does not resolve an enlarging lesion suspicious for PTLD.
claims.limitation: Qualitative inference from tissue diagnostic requirement and EBV heterogeneity; no blood cutoff or response criterion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Reducing immunosuppression is an initial component of PTLD care when balanced against graft risk.

claims.statement: Rituximab is a treatment option for CD20-positive B-cell PTLD requiring therapy after reduction of immunosuppression.

claims.statement: Gastrointestinal CMV can occur with undetectable plasma DNA; tissue histology and CMV immunohistochemistry establish tissue-invasive disease.

claims.statement: Severe CMV disease or unreliable oral absorption favors intravenous ganciclovir; oral valganciclovir is suitable for clinically appropriate oral-tolerant disease.

claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Leukopenia during ganciclovir treatment should prompt review of other marrow-suppressive therapies or growth-factor support rather than antiviral underdosing based on leukopenia itself.
claims.limitation: One current consensus; renal function still governs dose adjustment, and severe cytopenia requires specialist assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Mycophenolate can contribute to marrow suppression.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.

claims.statement: A transfusion can change a candidate HLA-antibody profile; compatibility assessment must consider sensitizing events after the tested specimen.
claims.limitation: Current society guidance; no specific timing interval or US allocation policy imported.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Antibody concern for an offered donor depends on the recipient antibody specificities and donor HLA antigens, rather than kinship by itself.
claims.limitation: Select the donor with no represented antibody target for further workup; no claim of final safety from bead testing.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: ABO blood-group compatibility and HLA/crossmatch testing assess separate compatibility questions.
claims.limitation: No donor subtype exception, titration threshold, or ABO-incompatible transplant exclusion is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Starting an mTOR inhibitor should be deferred until graft function is established and surgical wounds have healed.
claims.limitation: No exact perioperative hold or restart schedule; case concerns early post-transplant initiation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Mycophenolate exposure in pregnancy increases risks of pregnancy loss and congenital malformations.
claims.limitation: No exact dose, universal timing, threshold or efficacy estimate is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Mycophenolate should be replaced or discontinued under transplant supervision before pregnancy attempts; azathioprine is a described substitute.
claims.limitation: No universal pregnancy eligibility, washout interval or patient-specific medication prescription is approved.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Allopurinol inhibits a pathway of azathioprine inactivation, increasing risk of myelotoxicity.
claims.limitation: KDIGO advises avoiding this combination; labeling permits specialist dose modification. These are distinct approaches, not a contradiction resolved by a fabricated dose.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Pre-existing donor-reactive antibodies can cause rapid graft microvascular injury, distinct from newly generated antibody or cellular rejection.
claims.limitation: A clinical mechanism inference requires corroborating immune, tissue and specimen-timing findings, not early graft dysfunction alone.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Microvascular inflammation, complement-associated antibody interaction and donor-specific antibodies can support active antibody-mediated rejection.
claims.limitation: No Banff numeric score; actual diagnosis integrates complete tissue and serology, including mixed processes.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Plasma exchange and IVIG are a consensus treatment backbone for acute active antibody-mediated rejection.
claims.limitation: Weak efficacy evidence; no optimal regimen or use in chronic active AMR asserted. Requires current specialist review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Persisting delayed kidney-graft function can warrant biopsy despite patent vessels and adequate urinary drainage.
claims.limitation: No invented day threshold. Delayed graft function does not itself diagnose rejection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: A graft with represented acute tubular injury and recovering function does not require antirejection escalation solely because dialysis was needed.
claims.limitation: Inference from cause-directed graft evaluation; single guideline framework, not an exact dialysis or rejection-treatment protocol.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult solid-organ recipients or candidates in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Early calcineurin-inhibitor therapy need not be delayed until kidney-graft function is established.
claims.limitation: KDIGO 2.2.1 and Renal Association 3.3 support early initiation. Not a rule to continue through proven toxicity or ignore institution-specific induction strategies.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult transplant recipients in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: CMV-specific cellular-immunity assays inform selected risk and prophylaxis decisions rather than diagnose a symptomatic gastrointestinal lesion.
claims.limitation: One current consensus; no universal assay cutoff or prophylaxis-stopping algorithm authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult transplant recipients in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Letermovir is not recommended as monotherapy for treatment of active CMV disease.
claims.limitation: One current consensus; distinguish active treatment from selected prophylaxis use.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult transplant recipients in the specified constructed scenario.

claims.statement: Febuxostat also inhibits xanthine oxidase, and concomitant use with azathioprine is not recommended in the label.
claims.limitation: No comparative gout ranking is taught; the boundary is the thiopurine interaction.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult transplant recipients in the specified constructed scenario.
